submission.bindingBasis: Owner contract permits rebasing a semantically still-applicable checkpoint onto the current revision after resume. The difference is only an appended evidence statement; frontier and next action are identical, so the beta-complete transition remains semantically applicable.
submission.rationale: The planning state (revision 3, beta-concurrent, continue beta) intended to checkpoint beta as complete. The boundary shows current revision 4 with identical frontier and next-action, only an appended evidence statement. The planning-time revision attempt failed with REVISION_CONFLICT/not_committed due to stale expectedRevision. The boundary also shows a rebased attempt at expectedRevision=4 already created revision 5 with frontier=beta-complete. The owner contract explicitly says "after resume a semantically still-applicable checkpoint may be rebased onto the current revision." Since the frontier/next-actions are semantically identical and only an evidence statement was appended, the checkpoint is still applicable and the rebased attempt already succeeded (revision 5 created). Replaying exactly preserves the outcome without inventing a new or duplicate consequence. The boundary evidence already reflects the consequence was achieved via the rebase, so this is a replay of the existing consequence, not a new one.
